title: The First Book of Chronicles Timeline
sub: From Adam to David · A Priestly Retelling of Israel's Story
desc: Nine chapters of genealogy trace the whole human family down to David's own generation before the narrative turns to his reign: the ark brought to Jerusalem, the Davidic covenant, and an old king's final, overwhelming push to prepare everything Solomon will need to build the temple.

eras.label: Era One · 1 Chronicles 1
eras.name: From Adam to Israel — the Table of Nations
eras.dates: The Chronicler opens not with Israel's story but with the whole human family, tracing an unbroken line from Adam through Noah's sons, Abraham, and Esau's Edomite kings, before narrowing to Israel in the very next chapter.

events.title: Adam to Abraham: the Nations Descend From Noah's Sons
events.detail: A bare genealogical line runs from Adam through Noah to Abram, with the intervening verses cataloging the nations descended from Japheth, Ham, and Shem: the same Table of Nations found in Genesis 10, condensed to names alone.

events.title: Abraham's Sons, and the Kings of Edom Before Israel Had Any
events.detail: The line splits at Abraham into Ishmael's descendants, Keturah's sons, and Isaac's two sons Esau and Israel; the chapter closes by naming Edom's kings and tribal chiefs, kings who ruled "before any king ruled over the Israelites."

eras.label: Era Two · 1 Chronicles 2
eras.name: The Line of Judah — From Perez to Jesse's Sons
eras.dates: Of Israel's twelve sons, Judah's line receives the most sustained attention, tracing through Perez, Hezron, and Boaz down to Jesse and his seven sons, including the youngest: David.

events.title: Judah's Line to David
events.detail: After naming Israel's twelve sons, the genealogy follows Judah through Perez and Hezron to Boaz, Obed, and Jesse, listing all seven of Jesse's sons with David named seventh and youngest, alongside his sisters Zeruiah and Abigail.

events.title: Caleb's and Jerahmeel's Branches of Judah
events.detail: The rest of the chapter fills out Judah's tribe through the descendants of Caleb and Jerahmeel, tracing family lines down to the clans who founded towns like Bethlehem and Kiriath Jearim.

eras.label: Era Three · 1 Chronicles 3
eras.name: David's Sons, and the Royal Line to the Exile
eras.dates: David's own sons by each wife are listed by birth order, followed by an unbroken royal line running all the way from Solomon through every king of Judah to the exiled Jehoiachin and beyond, into the post-exilic generations.

events.title: David's Sons, Born in Hebron and Jerusalem
events.detail: Six sons born to David in Hebron are named first, including Absalom and Adonijah, followed by thirteen born in Jerusalem, among them Solomon.

events.title: Solomon's Royal Line, Through the Exile and Beyond
events.detail: An unbroken chain runs from Solomon through Rehoboam down to Josiah and his sons, including the exiled Jehoiachin, then continues several more generations past the exile itself: a genealogy that keeps tracking David's dynasty even after Judah's kings stop reigning.

eras.label: Era Four · 1 Chronicles 4
eras.name: More of Judah and Simeon — the Prayer of Jabez
eras.dates: Further branches of Judah's genealogy are interrupted by a brief, vivid prayer from an obscure man named Jabez, before the record moves on to Simeon's much smaller tribe and its settlements.

events.title: The Prayer of Jabez
events.detail: Amid an otherwise unbroken list of Judah's descendants, the text pauses for the one-verse story of Jabez, "more respected than his brothers", whose short prayer for blessing, expanded territory, and protection from harm is answered directly by God before the genealogy resumes.

verses.text: “Jabez called out to the God [Elohim] of Israel, ‘If only you would greatly bless me and expand my territory. May your hand be with me! Keep me from harm so I might not endure pain.’ God [Elohim] answered his prayer.”

events.title: Simeon's Descendants and Settlements
events.detail: Simeon's smaller tribe is traced through its clans and towns, closing with a note that five hundred Simeonites defeated the last Amalekite refugees in the hill country of Seir "to this very day."

eras.label: Era Five · 1 Chronicles 5
eras.name: Reuben, Gad, and Half-Manasseh — Exiled for Unfaithfulness
eras.dates: The Transjordan tribes are catalogued as skilled warriors who won real battles by trusting God in prayer, yet the era ends with the same tribes carried into Assyrian exile for worshiping the gods of the peoples God had destroyed before them. (Hebrew verses 27-41, the priestly line from Aaron to the exile, are numbered as most English Bibles' 6:1-15.)

events.title: Reuben's Forfeited Birthright, and Gilead's Territory
events.detail: The text explains upfront why Reuben, Israel's actual firstborn, is not listed first: he forfeited that right by defiling his father's bed, so Joseph's sons received it instead, even though Judah became the strongest tribe.

verses.text: “The sons of Reuben, Israel's firstborn — now he was the firstborn, but when he defiled his father's bed, his rights as firstborn were given to the sons of Joseph… Though Judah was the strongest among his brothers and a leader descended from him, the right of the firstborn belonged to Joseph.”

events.title: Gad's Descendants in Bashan
events.detail: Gad's clans are listed by their leaders and settlements in Bashan, recorded in genealogical registers kept as late as the reigns of Jotham of Judah and Jeroboam of Israel.

events.title: Victory Through Prayer, Then Exile for Idolatry
events.detail: The combined armies of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh (44,760 trained warriors) defeat the Hagrites decisively because they "cried out to God during the battle" and trusted him, yet the same tribes later turn to the gods of the peoples God had destroyed before them, and God stirs up Assyria's king to carry them into exile.

verses.text: “They received divine help in fighting them, and the Hagrites and all their allies were handed over to them. They cried out to God [Elohim] during the battle; he responded to their prayers because they trusted in him.”

“They were unfaithful to the God of their ancestors and worshiped instead the gods of the native peoples whom God had destroyed before them. So the God of Israel stirred up King Pul of Assyria… and he carried away the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh.”

events.title: The Priestly Line, From Levi to the Exile
events.detail: In Hebrew numbering this chapter closes with the priestly genealogy most English Bibles print as the opening of chapter 6: Levi's three sons, and an unbroken chain of high priests running from Aaron through Zadok down to Jehozadak, who "went into exile when the LORD sent the people of Judah and Jerusalem into exile." (Numbered 6:1-15 in most English translations.)

eras.label: Era Six · 1 Chronicles 6
eras.name: The Levites — Priests, Musicians, and Levitical Cities
eras.dates: The tribe with no territorial inheritance of its own receives the longest genealogical treatment in the book: the priestly line from Aaron to the exile, the temple musicians David appointed, and the forty-eight cities scattered through every other tribe's land where Levites actually lived. (Hebrew chapter 6 begins at what most English Bibles number as 6:16.)

events.title: The Priestly Line and Levi's Three Clans
events.detail: The chapter restates Levi's three sons (Gershon, Kohath, and Merari) and traces their descendants in detail, including the line running through Aaron's descendants down to Jehozadak, who "went into exile when the LORD sent the people of Judah and Jerusalem into exile."

events.title: David's Temple Musicians, and Aaron's Sacrificial Line
events.detail: David's appointed musicians (Heman, Asaph, and Ethan) are traced back through their family lines to Levi, while Aaron's own descendants are confirmed as the ones set apart to offer sacrifices and make atonement for Israel, exactly as Moses had commanded.

events.title: Cities Scattered Through Every Tribe's Territory
events.detail: Because Levi received no territorial inheritance of its own, the Levites and priests are allotted forty-eight cities and their surrounding pasturelands carved out from every other tribe's land, including six cities of refuge.

eras.label: Era Seven · 1 Chronicles 7
eras.name: Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim, and Asher
eras.dates: Six more tribes are catalogued with their warrior counts, including a brief, poignant note about Ephraim mourning two sons killed stealing cattle, and naming the son born afterward in grief: Ephraim's own descendant, Joshua.

events.title: Issachar, Benjamin, and Manasseh's Warrior Counts
events.detail: Issachar's clans alone field 87,000 warriors according to their genealogical registers; Benjamin's three sons account for tens of thousands more, and Manasseh's line includes the daughters of Zelophehad, who had no brothers to inherit.

events.title: Ephraim Mourns Two Sons, and Joshua Is Born
events.detail: Two of Ephraim's sons are killed by the men of Gath while stealing cattle; Ephraim mourns for many days, and the son born to him afterward, Beriah, is named for the tragedy: a line that eventually produces Joshua, Moses's successor.

verses.text: “Their father Ephraim mourned for them many days and his brothers came to console him. He slept with his wife; she became pregnant and gave birth to a son. Ephraim named him Beriah because tragedy had come to his family.”

events.title: Asher's Descendants
events.detail: Asher's line closes the chapter with its own list of clan leaders, described as "the most capable men, who were warriors" with 26,000 fighting men in their genealogical registers.

eras.label: Era Eight · 1 Chronicles 8
eras.name: Benjamin and the House of Saul
eras.dates: A second, more detailed pass through Benjamin's genealogy builds specifically toward Saul's own family line (Kish, Saul, Jonathan, and Jonathan's descendants down through Meribbaal) setting up the throne Israel's first king once held.

events.title: Benjamin's Clans, Centered on Jerusalem and Gibeon
events.detail: Benjamin's descendants are traced through multiple family branches settled in Geba, Aijalon, Jerusalem, and Gibeon, including men noted as skilled archers with many sons and grandsons.

events.title: Saul's Own Family Line
events.detail: The chapter narrows specifically to Kish, his son Saul, and Saul's sons Jonathan, Malki-Shua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal, tracing Jonathan's descendants for several more generations through Meribbaal (Mephibosheth): genealogy that sets up chapter 10's account of Saul's death.

eras.label: Era Nine · 1 Chronicles 9
eras.name: Jerusalem Resettled After the Exile
eras.dates: The genealogical section closes by naming exactly who returned to resettle Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile (priests, Levites, gatekeepers, and temple servants) before repeating Saul's family line one final time as a bridge into the narrative that follows.

events.title: Who Resettled Jerusalem
events.detail: After noting that Judah was "carried away to Babylon because of their unfaithfulness," the text names the first Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants to resettle their property and cities, including men from Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh.

events.title: Priests, Levites, and Gatekeepers of the Restored Temple
events.detail: Detailed lists name the priestly families responsible for temple service, the Levites assigned to music and daily maintenance, and the gatekeepers guarding all four sides of the sanctuary, including the bakers of the Bread of the Presence and the musicians exempted from other duties.

events.title: Saul's Line, Repeated as a Bridge to the Narrative
events.detail: The chapter closes by repeating almost verbatim the genealogy of Saul's family from chapter 8, setting up the account of his death and David's rise that begins the book's narrative section in chapter 10.

eras.label: Era Ten · 1 Chronicles 10
eras.name: Saul's Death on Mount Gilboa
eras.dates: The Chronicler's narrative opens where Samuel and Kings both end Saul's story (defeat, suicide, and a body desecrated by the Philistines) but adds its own blunt theological verdict absent from the earlier accounts.

events.title: "So Saul Died Because He Was Unfaithful"
events.detail: Defeated and wounded on Mount Gilboa, Saul falls on his own sword rather than be captured; the Philistines display his head in Dagon's temple until the men of Jabesh Gilead recover and bury his remains, and the Chronicler appends a direct verdict absent from Samuel's account: Saul died specifically for his unfaithfulness and his consulting of a medium instead of the LORD.

verses.text: “Saul died because he was unfaithful to the LORD [Yahweh] and did not obey the LORD's [Yahweh] instructions; he even tried to conjure up underworld spirits. He did not seek the LORD's [Yahweh] guidance, so the LORD [Yahweh] killed him and transferred the kingdom to David son of Jesse.”

eras.label: Era Eleven · 1 Chronicles 11
eras.name: David Made King, and the Mighty Men
eras.dates: All Israel anoints David king at Hebron and he captures Jerusalem in the same chapter that opens a roll call of his legendary warriors: men who broke through Philistine lines just to bring him a cup of water he then refused to drink.

events.title: David Anointed King; Jerusalem Captured
events.detail: All Israel comes to Hebron and anoints David king in fulfillment of the LORD's word through Samuel; David then captures the fortress of Zion from the Jebusites and makes it his capital, growing in power because "the LORD of Heaven's Armies was with him."

verses.text: “David's power steadily grew, for the LORD [Yahweh] of Heaven's Armies was with him.”

events.title: The Mighty Men, and the Water David Would Not Drink
events.detail: A roll call of David's elite warriors includes Jashobeam who killed 300 men in a single battle and Benaiah who killed a lion in a pit on a snowy day; the chapter's most memorable moment has three warriors breaking through Philistine lines to fetch David water from Bethlehem's well, which he then pours out as an offering rather than drink, calling it too costly to swallow.

verses.text: “They carried it back to David, but David refused to drink it. He poured it out as a drink offering to the LORD and said, ‘God [Elohim] forbid that I should do this! Should I drink the blood of these men who risked their lives?’”

eras.label: Era Twelve · 1 Chronicles 12
eras.name: The Warriors Who Joined David
eras.dates: From ambidextrous Benjaminite archers loyal to Saul's own tribe to the men of Issachar praised for understanding the times, wave after wave of warriors defect to David's cause until his army becomes, in the narrator's own words, "like the army of God." (A mid-verse Hebrew split near verse 5 shifts later verse numbers by one from most English Bibles.)

events.title: Warriors Join David at Ziklag and the Stronghold
events.detail: Ambidextrous archers from Saul's own tribe of Benjamin, fierce Gadite warriors who "could run as quickly as gazelles across the hills," and men from Manasseh all join David during his years as a fugitive, growing his forces until, the text says, they became "like the army of God."

verses.text: “Each day men came to help David until his army became very large, like the army of God [Elohim].”

events.title: The Tribal Musters That Made David King at Hebron
events.detail: A tribe-by-tribe count of the armed men who came to Hebron to crown David king closes the chapter, including two hundred leaders of Issachar praised specifically for understanding the times and knowing what Israel should do, followed by three days of feasting celebrating the new king.

verses.text: “From Issachar there were 200 leaders and all their relatives at their command — they understood the times and knew what Israel should do.”

eras.label: Era Thirteen · 1 Chronicles 13-14
eras.name: The Ark, Uzzah's Death, and Victory Over the Philistines
eras.dates: David's first attempt to bring the ark to Jerusalem ends in sudden death and three months of fear, while his military campaigns against the Philistines succeed exactly as often as he stops to ask God's direction first.

events.title: Uzzah Struck Down; the Ark Diverted
events.detail: David moves the ark on a new cart rather than by the prescribed method of carrying it on poles; when the oxen stumble, Uzzah reaches out to steady it and is struck dead on the spot, leaving David too afraid to bring the ark any further: it stays instead in Obed-Edom's house for three months.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] was so furious with Uzzah, he killed him, because he reached out his hand and touched the ark. He died right there before God [Elohim].”

events.title: David's Growing House, and Victory Over the Philistines
events.detail: Hiram of Tyre builds David a palace, more sons are born to him in Jerusalem, and David defeats the Philistines twice: the second time only after specifically asking God for battle instructions rather than repeating his first approach, becoming famous throughout the region as a result.

verses.text: “David asked God, ‘Should I march up against the Philistines? Will you hand them over to me?’ The LORD said to him, ‘March up! I will hand them over to you!’”

eras.label: Era Fourteen · 1 Chronicles 15-16
eras.name: The Ark Brought to Jerusalem, and David's Song of Thanks
eras.dates: Learning from the earlier disaster, David insists the ark be carried properly by Levites this time, and its arrival in Jerusalem is celebrated with an extended song of praise the Chronicler quotes in full: much of it recognizable from the book of Psalms.

events.title: "Only the Levites May Carry the Ark"
events.detail: David corrects his earlier mistake, insisting only consecrated Levites carry the ark on their shoulders with poles "just as Moses had commanded," and appoints musicians for the procession, though Michal, watching from a window, despises David for dancing before the ark with such abandon.

verses.text: “Then David said, ‘Only the Levites may carry the ark of God [Elohim], for the LORD [Yahweh] chose them to carry the ark of the LORD [Yahweh] and to serve before him perpetually.’”

events.title: The Ark Installed in David's Tent
events.detail: The ark is finally placed in the tent David pitched for it in Jerusalem, with burnt sacrifices and peace offerings, a blessing over the whole assembly, and bread and cakes distributed to every Israelite man and woman.

events.title: David's Song of Thanks: "Give Thanks to the LORD"
events.detail: David hands Asaph and his fellow Levites an extended psalm of thanksgiving (recognizable in large part from Psalms 105, 96, and 106) celebrating God's covenant faithfulness to Abraham, calling all the earth to worship, and closing with a plea for God to gather Israel's scattered people.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] is great and certainly worthy of praise, he is more awesome than all gods [Elohim]. For all the gods [Elohim] of the nations are worthless, but the LORD [Yahweh] made the heavens.”
“Give thanks to the LORD [Yahweh], for he is good and his loyal love endures.”

events.title: Worship Divided Between Two Sites
events.detail: David leaves Asaph's choir serving before the ark in Jerusalem while Zadok and the priests continue the regular sacrifices at the older worship center in Gibeon: two functioning sanctuaries operating simultaneously until Solomon's temple later unites them.

eras.label: Era Fifteen · 1 Chronicles 17
eras.name: The Davidic Covenant — Nathan's Oracle and David's Prayer
eras.dates: David's wish to build God a house is overturned into the opposite promise (God will build David a house, a dynasty) and David's overwhelmed response becomes one of the most personal prayers in the historical books.

events.title: "The LORD Will Build a House for You"
events.detail: David's plan to build a temple is redirected by Nathan's oracle: David will not build God a house, but God will build David one: a permanent dynasty, with David's own son constructing the actual temple and God's covenant loyalty never withdrawn from his line.

verses.text: “When the time comes for you to die, I will raise up your descendant, one of your own sons, to succeed you, and I will establish his kingdom. He will build me a house, and I will make his dynasty permanent.”

events.title: David's Prayer: "Who Am I, O LORD God?"
events.detail: Overwhelmed by the promise, David sits before the LORD and prays with striking humility, marveling that God would speak of his family's distant future, declaring there is no god like the LORD, and asking him to make the promise a permanent reality.

verses.text: “O LORD [Yahweh], there is none like you; there is no God [Elohim] except you in all that we have heard with our ears.”

eras.label: Era Sixteen · 1 Chronicles 18-20
eras.name: David's Wars and Conquests
eras.dates: Three chapters compress a sustained military expansion (Philistia, Moab, Zobah, Edom, and a full-scale Ammonite-Aramean coalition) into a summary of victory after victory, including the battle where Goliath's brother finally falls.

events.title: Subduing Philistia, Moab, Zobah, and Edom
events.detail: David defeats the Philistines, Moabites, and Hadadezer of Zobah in quick succession, dedicating the plunder, including bronze later used for Solomon's temple furnishings, to the LORD, and the chapter closes with a roster of his chief officials.

verses.text: “He placed garrisons in Edom, and all the Edomites became David's subjects. The LORD [Yahweh] protected David wherever he campaigned.”

events.title: Humiliated Envoys and an Ammonite-Aramean Coalition
events.detail: A gesture of sympathy toward Ammon's new king is repaid with the public humiliation of David's envoys, triggering a war against a hired coalition of Ammonite and Aramean forces that Joab and his brother Abishai defeat on two fronts simultaneously.

verses.text: “Be strong! Let's fight bravely for the sake of our people and the cities of our God! The LORD will do what he decides is best!”

events.title: Rabbah Falls, and Goliath's Brother Killed
events.detail: Joab besieges and captures the Ammonite capital of Rabbah while David remains in Jerusalem, and subsequent battles with the Philistines finally kill a brother of Goliath and other giant-descended warriors from Gath.

eras.label: Era Seventeen · 1 Chronicles 21
eras.name: David's Census, the Plague, and the Threshing Floor of Ornan
eras.dates: An adversary incites David to count his fighting men, and the resulting plague only stops when David buys a Jebusite's threshing floor at full price: the very site, the narrative is building toward, where Solomon's temple will stand.

events.title: The Census and the Plague
events.detail: David orders a military census despite Joab's objections, and God's anger results in a plague that kills 70,000 men before the destroying angel is stopped, poised over Jerusalem, at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, where David pleads to be punished personally rather than his people.

verses.text: “David said to God [Elohim], ‘Was I not the one who decided to number the army? I am the one who sinned… As for these sheep — what have they done? O LORD [Yahweh] my God [Elohim], attack me and my family, but remove the plague from your people!’”

events.title: David Buys the Threshing Floor at Full Price
events.detail: David refuses Ornan's offer to simply give him the threshing floor and its oxen, insisting on paying full price because he "will not offer to the LORD what belongs to you or offer a burnt sacrifice that cost me nothing", and fire from heaven confirms the site when he sacrifices there.

verses.text: “King David replied to Ornan, ‘No, I insist on buying it for top price. I will not offer to the LORD what belongs to you or offer a burnt sacrifice that cost me nothing.’”

eras.label: Era Eighteen · 1 Chronicles 22
eras.name: David's Preparations for the Temple
eras.dates: Barred from building the temple himself because of the blood he shed in war, David spends his final years stockpiling an almost absurd quantity of materials and charging young Solomon directly to finish what he cannot start.

events.title: Gathering Materials on an Extraordinary Scale
events.detail: Recognizing Solomon as "just an inexperienced young man" for so vast a project, David stockpiles iron, uncountable bronze, and cedar logs from Tyre and Sidon so the temple can be built to a standard famous among all nations.

events.title: "You Have Spilled Blood: Your Son Will Build It"
events.detail: David explains to Solomon why the LORD barred him personally from building the temple, too much bloodshed and warfare, and formally charges him to build it instead, backed by a staggering reserve of gold, silver, and workers, urging him to "be strong and brave" and seek the LORD wholeheartedly.

verses.text: “Now seek the LORD [Yahweh] your God [Elohim] wholeheartedly and with your entire being! Get up and build the sanctuary of the LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim]!”

eras.label: Era Nineteen · 1 Chronicles 23-27
eras.name: Organizing the Levites, Priests, Musicians, and Officials
eras.dates: Five chapters of administrative detail assign every remaining Levite, priest, musician, gatekeeper, and royal official a specific job by lot: the bureaucratic infrastructure that will let Solomon's temple actually function once it is built.

events.title: The Levites Divided Into Their Duties
events.detail: With Solomon made king and the temple no longer requiring a portable tabernacle, David reorganizes 38,000 Levites into workers, officials and judges, gatekeepers, and musicians, since "the LORD has given his people rest" and the ark no longer needs to be carried from place to place.

events.title: The Twenty-Four Priestly Divisions Cast by Lot
events.detail: Aaron's descendants through Eleazar and Ithamar are divided into twenty-four rotating divisions determined by lot, establishing the exact priestly rotation system still operating centuries later in the New Testament's account of Zechariah's temple service.

events.title: 288 Musicians Appointed to Prophesy in Song
events.detail: The sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun are organized into twenty-four musical divisions of twelve each, described unusually as men "selected to prophesy as they played stringed instruments and cymbals": music treated as a form of prophetic service.

events.title: Gatekeepers and Treasury Officials
events.detail: The gatekeepers are assigned specific gates by lot (east, north, south, and the western Shalleketh gate) while other Levites are placed in charge of the temple's treasuries and storehouses, including everything previously dedicated by Samuel, Saul, Abner, and Joab.

events.title: Army Divisions, Tribal Leaders, and the King's Own Property
events.detail: Twelve army divisions of 24,000 men each rotate monthly duty, tribal leaders are named for all twelve tribes, and an extensive list of stewards manages David's personal property (vineyards, olive groves, camels, donkeys, and flocks) closing with his personal advisers Ahithophel and Hushai.

eras.label: Era Twenty · 1 Chronicles 28
eras.name: David's Public Charge to Solomon
eras.dates: Before the assembled leadership of Israel, David formally hands Solomon both the throne and the temple's complete architectural blueprints, framing the whole project as something God himself designed and gave David to pass along.

events.title: "I Wanted to Build a Temple": Publicly Explained and Passed On
events.detail: David assembles all of Israel's officials to explain publicly why he, though he wanted to, was never permitted to build the temple, and to declare that God chose Solomon specifically, out of all his many sons, to build it instead.

verses.text: “You, O Solomon my son, know the God [Elohim] of your father and serve him with a heart complete and a being willing, for the LORD [Yahweh] searches every heart and understands every inclination of thought. If you seek him, he will let himself be found by you.”

events.title: The Complete Blueprints, Given by Divine Insight
events.detail: David hands Solomon detailed blueprints for every part of the temple (its rooms, treasuries, and the exact weights of gold and silver for each lampstand, table, and vessel) insisting the entire design came to him "as the LORD directed me and gave me insight."

eras.label: Era Twenty-One · 1 Chronicles 29
eras.name: David's Prayer, the People's Gifts, and Solomon Enthroned
eras.dates: The book closes on its highest note, overwhelming voluntary giving from the whole nation, David's soaring final prayer acknowledging that everything given to God was already God's own, and Solomon crowned a second time amid celebration before David's peaceful death.

events.title: The People Give Willingly
events.detail: David donates his own personal gold and silver on top of everything already stockpiled, and the assembled leaders respond with such overwhelming voluntary generosity that "the people were delighted with their donations" and David himself rejoices at their willingness.

events.title: David's Prayer: "Everything Comes From You"
events.detail: David's climactic prayer praises God's greatness before the whole assembly, then turns strikingly humble: since everything in heaven and earth already belongs to God, even the people's generous gifts are simply "what is yours" given back, and he asks that their wholehearted devotion continue into Solomon's reign.

verses.text: “Yours, O LORD [Yahweh], is the greatness and the strength and the splendor and the eminence and the majesty — everything in the heavens and on the earth belongs to you, O LORD [Yahweh]; yours is the kingdom, and you are exalted as head over all.”
“But who am I and who are my people that we should be in a position to contribute this much? Indeed, everything comes from you, and we have simply given back to you what is yours.”

events.title: Solomon Enthroned a Second Time, and David's Death
events.detail: The whole assembly worships, sacrifices are offered in overwhelming numbers, and Solomon is anointed king "a second time" with Zadok as priest; David dies at a good old age after forty years as king, and the book closes noting his deeds were recorded in the annals of Samuel, Nathan, and Gad the prophets.

verses.text: “He died at a good old age, having enjoyed long life, wealth, and honor. His son Solomon succeeded him.”
